notes: REAL ERROR IN THE UNFLAGGED STRATUM, and an instructive one: it is NOT the usual claimant-for-grantee slip. Here the U.S.-era claimant IS the Mexican grantee (Wolfskill claimed under a grant made to himself), so the register's own patent_to field, 'William Wolfskill', holds the correct grantee while the grantee field holds an unrelated name. Hoffman 1862 prints the same wrong grantee (Francisco Guerrero) for court no. 232, which is exactly why this record came through unflagged: the two secondary sources agree with each other and both disagree with the case file. Any other register rows whose grantee traces to Hoffman alone deserve the same treatment. Corroboration outside the file: the digicoll record for 256566 lists 'Wolfskill, William, 1798-1866' as Claimant, Grantee AND Patentee, and its Bowman abstract reads 'Granted by Alvarado May 24, 1842, to William Wolfskill'. outcome.evidence: final disposition is confirmation, but ONLY by reversal. The Board REJECTED: transcript docket, stamped p.4 (image 10): 'San Francisco October 31' 1854. In the same Case Commissioner Alpheus Felch delivered the opinion of the Board rejecting the claim. (Vide page 19 of this Transcript.)'. The claimants appealed (notice filed 12 July 1855, stamped p.86, image 103). The District Court then found for them: Supreme Court mandate, stamped p.106 (image 123), recites 'in the District Court ... in a cause between Valentin Cota [et al] appellants, and The United States appellees, (No. 231, for "Rio de Santa Clara") wherein the decree was rendered in favor of the said appellants'. The United States' appeal from that decree was killed at stamped p.108 (image 125): 'in the present term of December ... one thousand eight hundred and sixty three the said cause came on to be heard before the said Supreme Court ... on the motion of Mr Attorney General Bates of counsel for the Appellants, it is now here considered, ordered and decreed by this Court that this cause be and the same is hereby dismissed'; mandate No. 164, December Term 1863, teste Roger B. Taney, filed 18 Feb 1864 (stamped p.109, image 126).

notes: THIS IS THE TEXTBOOK CASE OF THE 'Confirmed' TRAP, and the register survives it: the Land Commission rejected this claim outright on 31 Oct 1854, and the register's 'Confirmed' is true only because the District Court reversed and the Supreme Court then dismissed the government's appeal in the December 1863 term. Unlike rancho-arroyo-seco-1, the whole chain is inside this ONE volume (the file selector lists only cubanc_lcf_sd231), so no volume is unread and the grade is earned rather than guessed. Why it went unflagged is now obvious: Hoffman's 1862 table prints disposition 'confirmed' and patented=false, which is exactly right as of 1862 - the DC decree had been entered, the appeal was still pending, and the patent did not issue until 1872. GROUND OF THE REJECTION, worth recording because it bears on 1836-37 grants generally: the U.S. Attorney's answer, stamped p.94 (image 111), pleads 'That Juan B. Alvarado, calling himself the Governor of the free and Sovereign State of Upper California, and President of the most excellent Deputation, had no lawful authority on the 22nd of May 1837, to grant the land claimed'; the claimants' 1855 affidavit, stamped p.103 (image 120), states the Commission rejected because 'the Sovereignty of which Alvarado was the head at the time of the grant was made, did not reach the dignity of a de facto government'. The register's 'Alvarado / 1837' is nonetheless exactly what the instrument says. Other pleaded grounds: land within ten leagues of the sea coast without previous consent of the supreme government; occupied by Mission San Buenaventura; no Departmental Assembly approval. notes: SECOND REAL ERROR, and this one IS the dominant class the audit was built to catch: the U.S.-era claimant sitting in the Mexican grantee slot. Hoffman 1862 leaves both governor and grantee BLANK for court no. 201, so whoever filled this register row had no Hoffman value to copy and appears to have taken the name off the case label ('JAMES BLAIR, ET AL CLAIMANT'), which is exactly the failure mode. Note the internal tell the register missed: its own patent_to reads 'John P. Davison et al' - Blair's co-claimants - so the register has a claimant in the grantee field and a different set of claimants in the patentee field, with the actual grantee nowhere. CHAIN OF TITLE in the file, useful for the correction: Francisco de Haro held Salsipuedes and conveyed his right to Jimeno 26 Feb 1831 (Exhibit A, stamped p.17, image 25; Hartnell's deposition, stamped p.12, image 18, says de Haro 'sold it to Manuel Jimeno' in 1831 or 1832); Figueroa granted to Jimeno 4 Nov 1834 (two square leagues); Territorial Deputation approved 29 Aug 1835; Alvarado augmented to eight square leagues 1 Feb 1840 and ratified 1 Mar 1840; Micheltorena ratified 1 Apr 1843 notwithstanding the land lying within ten littoral leagues; Jimeno sold to the present claimants 11 Oct 1852 (Jimeno's own deposition, stamped p.11, image 17: 'I occupied the said Rancho from the year 1831 until the year 1852 in which last year I sold it to the present claimants'). The register's 1834/Figueroa correctly follows the ORIGINAL concession rather than the 1840 Alvarado augmentation - worth flagging only because a different register might reasonably have chosen 1840. PROCEDURAL DETAIL: on 27 Dec 1853 the Board granted leave to substitute the heirs of the petitioner (stamped p.3, image 8), i.e. Blair had died; on 26 Dec 1854 Commissioner Felch overruled a later claimants' motion of 19 Sept 1854 and denied that petition (stamped p.4, image 9) - an ancillary motion, not a rejection of the claim, which had already been confirmed 2 May 1854. ORTHOGRAPHY: the clerk wrote the place as 'Val si puedes' on the docket leaf, stamped p.2 (image 7), while the grant papers write 'Salsipuedes'.
